Contributing to rmoriebricklayer

Source: CONTRIBUTING.md

Thanks for considering a contribution. This package lives or dies by being boring and reliable: a reviewer should never wonder why something is the way it is.

Reporting bugs and asking for features

Open an issue at https://github.com/rootcoder007/rmorie-bricklayer/issues. Include the output of sessionInfo(), the smallest code that shows the problem, and what you expected. Issues and pull requests are public and searchable; reports are welcome in English.

Security problems go through the private route in SECURITY.md, never a public issue.

Scope

In scope:

  • Cross-platform fixes (Linux, macOS, Windows, non-UTF-8 locales)
  • New data-source resolvers (Dataverse, Zenodo, plain HTTPS); see docs/data_sources.md
  • New synthetic-column types in R/lib_synthetic.R
  • Clearer error messages, especially first-run failures
  • Documentation, examples and vignettes

Out of scope (politely declined):

  • New hard dependencies outside base R (the package imports only base R)
  • Required cloud services, sign-ins, telemetry or analytics
  • Docker or any other container as a required step

How a change gets in

  1. Fork the repository and branch from main.
  2. Make the change, with tests (below).
  3. Run the checks in the next section.
  4. Open a pull request that says what changed and why, and paste the check output. CI runs on every pull request; it must be green before merge.
  5. The maintainer reviews every pull request. main keeps a linear history, so changes are rebased, not merged.

Requirements for an acceptable change

  • Tests. Every new function, argument or behaviour comes with testthat tests in tests/testthat/, and every bug fix with a test that fails before the fix. Coverage of changed lines is checked on each pull request.
  • Documentation. Exported functions have roxygen2 documentation with @param, @return and a runnable @examples block; run roxygen2::roxygenise() and commit the man/ changes. User-visible changes get a bullet in NEWS.md.
  • Style. Base R, lines of at most 80 characters, ASCII-only R sources (use \u escapes). lintr::lint_package() must report nothing (the rules are in .lintr), and goodpractice::gp() must stay clean.
  • C and C++. No new compiler warnings in R CMD check --as-cran; the sanitizer and constant-time workflows must stay green. Changes under src/ also need the fuzz targets to build (inst/fuzz/build.sh).
  • Cryptography. Only published, standardised algorithms (FIPS 202-205, RFC 8391, SP 800-90A, RFC 3161). Changes to these files need the matching known-answer vectors to pass (tests/testthat/test-vectors-*.R).

Checks to run before a pull request

R CMD build .
R CMD check --as-cran rmoriebricklayer_*.tar.gz
Rscript -e 'lintr::lint_package()'

R CMD check runs the full test suite. For a quicker loop while working:

devtools::test()

If the change touches R/lib_synthetic.R or the synthesis recipe schema, also run the end-to-end bundle test:

./dev/test_build_otis.sh
./dev/test_build_otis.sh --with-data /path/to/a01_RC.csv

Code of conduct

This project is released with a Contributor Code of Conduct; by taking part you agree to abide by its terms. In short: be kind. The audience is graduate students and reviewers. If an error message is unclear, fix the error message.

Licence

By contributing, you agree your contribution is licensed under AGPL-3.0-or-later, the same as the rest of the project.
